success_criteria.description: All four districts are in use and every precinct is assigned.
All four districts have roughly equal population (within 15%).

character.name: You
character.motivation: The whole toolkit, one map — bigger, four districts, everything on the table at once. Draw a legal map, read the result, and you've got the fundamentals cold.

intro_slides.body: This is the whole kit. Fairhaven is bigger — four districts — and nothing is hidden: the Map Validity panel, the Lean view, the County borders, and the election result are all here from the start. Draw a legal map and watch what it produces.
intro_slides.heading: Everything You've Learned

intro_slides.body: A legal map is the same as ever: four districts, roughly equal in population, each one connected. The Map Validity panel tracks both — even the districts out and keep each whole until it's green. There's no seat target; read the result to see who your lines elect, then submit. Get this down and the maps ahead are the same craft with new twists.
intro_slides.heading: A Complete Legal Map

narrative.objective: Draw four balanced, connected districts — a complete legal map — and read the result your lines produce, then submit. (No seat target; the outcome is yours to read, not to hit.)
narrative.epilogue:
That's everything: pick a district and paint it, keep the populations even and each district whole, and read the lean and the result to see who your lines elect. You've got the whole loop now.
Every race so far has come down to two sides. Next the map opens up — a third party with ground of its own to hold, then a candidate who answers to no party. Same tools, more corners to weigh. On to the three-way race.
